articles.title: Effects of Packaging and Food Waste Prevention by Consumers on the Environmental Impact of Production and Consumption of Bread in Norway

functional_unit.base: bread produced, distributed and consumed in Norway

articles.title: Wasting of Fresh-Packed Bread by Consumers—Influence of Shopping Behavior, Storing, Handling, and Consumer Preferences
articles.measure: Respondent-estimated slices of fresh bread wasted from household per week

transcription_verification.method: Independent reading of text extracted from the archived PDF bytes using pdftotext -layout; no network source was fetched.
transcription_verification.survey_table_check: All seven labels, counts and reported percentages in survey_table1.json agree with PDF page 4 Table 1; the methodological prose on PDF page 3 lists different interval boundaries.

exposure.scope: The articles, quantitative inputs and previously archived table were exposed before this package was prepared. The neutral transcription adds published milling, gas and allocation entries from the same local articles.
exposure.freeze_rule: Freeze task, transcription, manifest and external evaluator rubric in an identified Git revision before the new executions.

limits: Company aggregates and secondary calculations do not identify a single observed lot across stages.
Table 7 uses the common published base Bread Entering the System; its rows are not observations of sequential conditional loss rates.
Milling mass fractions and economic allocation factors have different meanings and bases.
Bakery energy is reported per loaf; mill electricity is reported per tonne of flour, not per tonne of wheat.
The survey concerns self-reported household weekly discard, not personal intake, weighed waste or identified consumers of the LCA product.
Table 1 contains an open upper category and a do-not-know category; no slice mass, consumption denominator or finite upper cap is supplied.
Only category frequencies are archived as structured data, not respondent-level records or current operational observations.
These sources cannot establish the causal efficacy or safety of a proposed packaging change.
